newsitem.title: UK: BA down further after analyst briefing.
newsitem.headline: BA down further after analyst briefing.

text.p: Shares in British Airways Plc extended earlier losses by late afternoon on Monday, as analysts lowered earnings estimates in the wake of a post-results briefing with analysts, dealers said.
The stock was down 30-1/2p at 609-1/2 by 1515 GMT, in active trade of 6.4 million shares.

BA shares were under pressure from the outset, after first quarter profits fell short of analyst expectations and dealers noted there was no positive news on the company's planned alliance with American Airlines.

Chris Avery, analyst at Paribas Capital Markets, said he now expected underlying pre-tax profits to fall by 100 million stg to around 395 million stg in the current year, whereas he had been looking for profit improvement.
Avery said the move largely reflected the greater-than-expected impact of sterling strength as well as strike action by some BA staff.
BA posted a 46.7 percent rise in first-quarter pre-tax profit to 220 million stg, yet that total was boosted by a 130 million stg gain on the sale of its US Airways stake.

The underlying result fell short of analyst expectations, which had ranged mostly between 115 million stg and 151 million. BA said the strength of sterling had taken a 77 million chunk out of its profits.

The company said regulatory approval of its proposed alliance with American Airlines was proceeding very slowly, adding that last month's cabin crew strike would cost it a further 125 million stg, well above analysts' previous expectations.

Analyst Chris Gunn at Credit Lyonnais Laing said he expected current year pre-tax profit estimates before exceptional items to come down to between 500 million stg and 510 million, from 580-600 million stg.
Gunn said BA was facing a rising tax change and capital spending of around two billion stg a year, as well as higher-than-expected currency and strike costs.
"For the first time in ages, BA looks as if it is on the back foot," Gunn said.
He said the market would probably react positively if BA secured even a watered-down deal with American Airlines, yet cost savings would be harder to quantify in such a situation.
By the close, BA shares were down 29-1/2p at 610-1/2, the lowest close since February 17.
